children: Six more companies, including Wells Fargo
, have told a joint venture of crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange
that they will not allow their shares to be tokenized on its platform, Reuters reported Friday.
The objections had not been reported before and bring the total to 22, the document shows. It does not say why the companies objected.

OKX and ICE planned to tokenize 63 stocks through the venture, called OKXICE, and filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month to launch under the agency’s new innovation exemption. The exemption requires platforms to notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their stock, and bars them from going ahead if an issuer objects. Tokenized shares must carry the same rights as traditional ones, including dividends and voting.

Reuters said the objections highlight the growing challenges facing tokenization, the creation of digital tokens that represent a stock and trade on a blockchain like cryptocurrencies, even after the SEC’s recent approval of the products.
The newest names follow earlier objections from Microsoft
, according to Crypto Briefing. The objections apply to the OKXICE venue, the outlet noted, and do not necessarily mean the companies oppose every form of stock tokenization.
Arm and Intuit did not immediately provide comment, Reuters said. A Wells Fargo spokesperson declined to comment.
